paragraphs.text: Imagine a fluid that conducts electricity, like the liquid iron deep inside the Earth.
When it moves, it drags {b}magnetic field{/} lines along, as if they were frozen into it.
Stretch a field line, and the field gets stronger.
On one side, the {u}flow{/} stretches and folds the field.
On the other, diffusion lets it leak away.
Their ratio is the magnetic Reynolds number, {param}Rm{/}.
In three dimensions, even a simple flow, the ABC flow, can win this tug of war.
Above a critical value of Rm, a magnetic field grows on its own: a dynamo.
In the three-mode model of Gissinger, reversals of the field switch on as the parameter grows.
The generative model, trained on a few values, reproduces the whole curve.
The first test bench sweeps the magnetic diffusivity over eleven values; these results are still being computed.
